Before you start · 10 minutes

Map your columns to the names this guide uses

Every query and measure below uses the standard names on the right. Her files keep their own headers: the ColumnMap table translates them once, so nothing else in the guide needs editing. Use column names and file types only. No customer rows are needed to set this up.

Map The nine columns the dashboard needs

Standard nameHoldsTypeNeeded forHer header
As_Of_DateDate of the snapshot. If the file has no such column, the date is read from the file name.DateEvery trend and comparisonAS OF DATE
PN_NoPromissory note number. One loan.TextLoan key; new / cured / rolledPN NO.
Borrower_IDBorrower or CIF numberTextTop 10 labelsBORROWER ID
BranchBooking branchTextSlicer, branch chartsBRANCH
Account_OfficerAssigned AOTextSlicerACCOUNT OFFICER
Loan_ProductProduct name or codeTextSlicer, product chartsLOAN PRODUCT
PSIC_SectionPSIC 2009 section letter (A to U)TextIndustry pagePSIC SECTION
Outstanding_BalanceBalance used for delinquency ratios, in pesosFixed decimalEvery ₱ figureOUTSTANDING BALANCE
Days_Past_DueDays past due at end of day. Blank or 0 = current.Whole numberEvery DPD figureDAYS PAST DUE

The last column is a placeholder. Replace it with her real headers in the ColumnMap query below.

Code ColumnMap query

  1. Home › New Source › Blank Query › Advanced Editor. Paste this, name it ColumnMap, right-click › untick Enable load.
  2. Change only the left column. Spacing and case do not matter. Two left names may point to one right name when a header changed over the years.
ColumnMap · Power Query M
// ColumnMap: left = the header as it appears in her files (any case, any spacing);
// right = the name this guide uses. Several left names may point to one right name
// (a header renamed over the years). Leave a left name "" if her files lack that column:
// that column then loads empty.
let
    Source = #table(
        type table [Her_Column = text, Standard_Column = text],
        {
            {"AS OF DATE",          "As_Of_Date"},
            {"PN NO.",              "PN_No"},
            {"PN NUMBER",           "PN_No"},
            {"BORROWER ID",         "Borrower_ID"},
            {"BRANCH",              "Branch"},
            {"ACCOUNT OFFICER",     "Account_Officer"},
            {"LOAN PRODUCT",        "Loan_Product"},
            {"PSIC SECTION",        "PSIC_Section"},
            {"OUTSTANDING BALANCE", "Outstanding_Balance"},
            {"O/S BALANCE",         "Outstanding_Balance"},
            {"DAYS PAST DUE",       "Days_Past_Due"},
            {"DPD",                 "Days_Past_Due"}
        })
in
    Source

Why The logic

One translation table instead of renames inside each query. When the core-banking extract renames a header, she edits one row here. Every query, measure and visual below keeps working.

  • Nine columns, nothing more. Each one feeds a visual or a key. Extra columns slow every refresh and widen what a dashboard user can see.
  • The balance must be the one Credit Risk uses for the ratio: principal only, or principal plus accrued interest. If the two differ, the dashboard will not tie to the aging report.

Confirm Before management sees a number

  1. "1–30 DPD" means 1 to 30 days past due, counted from the oldest unpaid due date, the same as the bank's aging report and the BSP past-due definition it reports under.
  2. Ratios are by balance (₱), not by account count.
  3. Closed, paid-off and written-off loans have no row or a zero balance. Zero-balance rows are dropped.
  4. The weekly position is the first business day of each week (Tuesday when Monday is a holiday).
  5. PSIC holds the section letter. If her files carry the 4- or 5-digit class code instead, add a class-to-section lookup before Step 2.
  6. Branch, Officer, Product and Industry use each loan's latest value, so history is shown under today's branch.

Folder: C:\Bank\LoanDaily\ holding one extract per business day, named with the date (loans_20261019.xlsx). Placeholder path and names.

Do Steps

  1. Home › Manage Parameters › New: name FolderPath, type Text, current value = her folder path with the trailing backslash. Or paste the parameter code into a blank query.
  2. New blank query Files: paste the code. Untick Enable load (it holds file contents, not data for the model).
  3. Save each extract with the date in the file name as yyyymmdd. Step 2 reads the date from there when the file has no as-of column.
  4. DataFiles keeps .xlsx and .csv, and skips Excel lock files (~$…) and hidden files. Save an old .xls as .xlsx first.

Why The logic

A parameter, not a typed path. When the folder moves to a shared drive or SharePoint, she changes one value. On the Power BI Service the parameter can be edited without opening Desktop.

  • The filters stop the classic refresh failures: an Excel file left open writes a hidden ~$ copy, and a stray .pdf or .msg in the folder breaks Excel.Workbook.
  • Sorted newest first so Files{0} is always the latest file. Step 2 tests against it and Step 3 keeps the newest copy when a date is sent twice.
  • Not loaded. Binary content in the model adds size and nothing a visual can use.
  • Scheduled refresh on the Service: a C:\ or network-drive folder refreshes only through an on-premises data gateway that can reach that path. A SharePoint folder needs no gateway.
  • SharePoint later: replace Folder.Files(FolderPath) with SharePoint.Files(site, [ApiVersion = 15]) and filter on Folder Path. Nothing downstream changes.

Code Paste into Advanced Editor

FolderPath · Power Query M
// FolderPath: the one folder every daily extract is saved into. Change the path here only.
"C:\Bank\LoanDaily\" meta [IsParameterQuery = true, Type = "Text", IsParameterQueryRequired = true]
Files · Power Query M
// Files: every daily extract in FolderPath (and its subfolders), newest file name first
let
    Source = Folder.Files(FolderPath),
    DataFiles = Table.SelectRows(Source, each
        List.Contains({".xlsx", ".csv"}, Text.Lower([Extension]))
        and not Text.StartsWith([Name], "~$")
        and [Attributes]?[Hidden]? <> true),
    Kept = Table.SelectColumns(DataFiles, {"Content", "Name", "Extension", "Date modified", "Folder Path"}),
    Sorted = Table.Sort(Kept, {{"Name", Order.Descending}})
in
    Sorted

Drawn to match Power Query in Power BI Desktop. Sample rows, not real accounts.

Do Steps

  1. Home › New Source › Blank Query › Advanced Editor. Paste fnCleanFile below and name the query fnCleanFile. It reads ColumnMap from Step 0.
  2. Add a second blank query named Check_OneFile with the code below (its formula is shown in the picture). It runs the function on the first file only, so you can test the cleaning before stacking a year of files.
  3. Check the type icon on every column header: date, text, ₱ fixed decimal, whole number. An ABC on a money column means the header did not map; fix it in ColumnMap, not here.
  4. Source_File is on every row. Keep it: it is how you trace any number on the dashboard back to the file it came from.
  5. Click through the applied steps from Raw to Tagged. Row count should drop only at RealRows (totals, blank lines and repeated headers removed).
  6. If her extracts have title lines above the header row, add Table.Skip(Raw, n) before Headers. For CSV, Power Query sizes the columns from the first line, so title lines also cost columns: open those with [Columns = 12] (her column count) in Csv.Document.

Why The logic

A function, not the built-in Combine Files helper. The helper builds hidden "Sample File" and "Transform Sample File" queries that break when the first file in the folder changes or is removed. A named function you wrote is visible, testable and does not depend on which file sorts first.

  • Headers are cleaned before they are mapped because core-banking extracts drift: a trailing space, a hidden line break or a change of case is enough to drop a column without an error.
  • Renaming uses MissingField.Ignore, selecting uses MissingField.UseNull. A file missing a column still loads with blanks instead of failing the whole refresh; the Step 3 checks then show which file was short.
  • Report noise is dropped by PN No. Any line whose PN contains TOTAL (subtotal, branch total, grand total) would count the book twice, and a header row repeated mid-file would break typing. A PN No. is the one field a real loan row always has.
  • PN No. is upper-cased. Power Query groups "pn-1" and "PN-1" as two loans; the model treats them as one and the relationship breaks.
  • Types use the "en-PH" culture so "18,450,000.00" reads as a number and 10/19/2026 as 19 October. Typing without a culture uses the PC's regional setting, which differs between machines.
  • Blank DPD becomes 0 only after typing, because the extract leaves current accounts blank. A blank would drop the loan out of every "Current" count.

Code Paste into Advanced Editor

fnCleanFile · Power Query M
// fnCleanFile: cleans ONE daily loan file. Step 3 calls it once per file in the folder.
(FileContent as binary, Extension as text, FileName as text) as table =>
let
    // 1. Open the file by type: first worksheet of an Excel file, or a CSV
    Raw = if Text.Lower(Extension) = ".csv"
        then Csv.Document(FileContent, [Delimiter = ",", Encoding = 65001, QuoteStyle = QuoteStyle.Csv])
        else Table.SelectRows(Excel.Workbook(FileContent, null, true), each [Kind] = "Sheet"){0}[Data],
    Headers = Table.PromoteHeaders(Raw, [PromoteAllScalars = true]),

    // 2. Same header spelling every day: trim, remove hidden characters, upper case
    CleanNames = Table.TransformColumnNames(Headers, each Text.Upper(Text.Trim(Text.Clean(_)))),

    // 3. Her column names -> standard names, from the ColumnMap table (Step 0)
    MapPairs = List.Select(List.Transform(Table.ToRecords(ColumnMap), each {Text.Upper(Text.Trim([Her_Column])), [Standard_Column]}), each _{0} <> ""),
    Renamed = Table.RenameColumns(CleanNames, MapPairs, MissingField.Ignore),
    Kept = Table.SelectColumns(Renamed, List.Distinct(ColumnMap[Standard_Column]), MissingField.UseNull),

    // 4. Drop report noise: blank rows, any TOTAL line (TOTAL, SUBTOTAL, GRAND TOTAL, BRANCH TOTAL),
    //    and header rows repeated inside the file
    HeaderNames = List.Transform(ColumnMap[Her_Column], each Text.Upper(Text.Trim(_))),
    RealRows = Table.SelectRows(Kept, each
        let p = if [PN_No] = null then "" else Text.Upper(Text.Trim(Text.From([PN_No]))) in
            p <> "" and not Text.Contains(p, "TOTAL") and not List.Contains(HeaderNames, p)),

    // 5. As-of date: from the file's own column, else from the 8 digits in the file name (loans_20261019.xlsx)
    FileDate = try Date.FromText(Text.Start(Text.Select(FileName, {"0".."9"}), 8), [Format = "yyyyMMdd"]) otherwise null,
    WithDate = Table.ReplaceValue(RealRows, null, FileDate, Replacer.ReplaceValue, {"As_Of_Date"}),

    // 6. Types, read the Philippine way (commas in amounts, month/day/year dates)
    Typed = Table.TransformColumnTypes(WithDate, {
        {"As_Of_Date", type date}, {"PN_No", type text}, {"Borrower_ID", type text},
        {"Branch", type text}, {"Account_Officer", type text}, {"Loan_Product", type text},
        {"PSIC_Section", type text}, {"Outstanding_Balance", Currency.Type},
        {"Days_Past_Due", Int64.Type}}, "en-PH"),

    // 7. Text tidy-up: PN No. trimmed and upper case (the model matches keys ignoring case, Power Query does not),
    //    blank industry -> "N/A" (consumer loans carry no PSIC)
    Trimmed = Table.TransformColumns(Typed, {
        {"PN_No", each Text.Upper(Text.Trim(_)), type text}, {"Borrower_ID", each if _ = null then null else Text.Trim(_), type text},
        {"PSIC_Section", each if _ = null or Text.Trim(_) = "" then "N/A" else Text.Upper(Text.Trim(_)), type text}}),
    NoNullDPD = Table.ReplaceValue(Trimmed, null, 0, Replacer.ReplaceValue, {"Days_Past_Due"}),

    // 8. Keep the file name on every row, so any number can be traced back to its file
    Tagged = Table.AddColumn(NoNullDPD, "Source_File", each FileName, type text)
in
    Tagged
Check_OneFile · Power Query M
// Check_OneFile: runs the cleaning on the newest file only. Not loaded to the model.
let
    Source = fnCleanFile(Files{0}[Content], Files{0}[Extension], Files{0}[Name])
in
    Source

Sample figures. The highlighted date has two files: the 12-row resend is the question to raise with the data owner.

Do Steps

  1. New blank queries Loan_Files and Loan_All: paste the code. Untick Enable load on both. Loan_All is the one stacked table the model tables are cut from in Step 4.
  2. New blank query Check_Files: paste the code. Untick Enable load. Open it after every refresh.
  3. Read Check_Files top down: Rows close to the day before; Total_Balance moves by less than the day's releases and collections; Blank_Balance 0; Files_Same_Date 1. Rows 0 means an empty or unreadable file.
  4. Tie the newest Total_Balance to the GL loan total for that date before building anything on it.

Why The logic

Clean first, then stack. Each file is made identical before Table.Combine, so a header renamed in March cannot split one column into two half-empty ones.

  • Deduplicate on PN No. plus date. A file sent twice would double the book for that day. The key is the loan-day, so a genuine new loan is never dropped. Files are sorted newest name first and the stack keeps that order, so the latest copy is kept in practice; Power Query does not promise it, so check Source_File by hand on any date Check_Files flags.
  • Rows with no date are dropped: a file with neither an as-of column nor a date in its name cannot be placed on the timeline. It shows as missing in Check_Files.
  • Check_Files reads the files before duplicates are removed, so a full resend still shows as two files for one date, and an empty file shows as 0 rows.
  • Check_Files is the audit trail. Each dashboard number traces to Source_File. When a manager asks why the ratio jumped, the first answer is whether the file was complete.
  • Staging is not loaded. Only the four model tables in Step 4 reach the model, so the stacked text columns are not stored twice. Each model query reads the folder again, so a refresh parses every file several times: keep 13 months in the folder and archive the rest.

Code Paste into Advanced Editor

Loan_Files · Power Query M
// Loan_Files: one row per file, its cleaned rows nested in [Data]. Staging only: not loaded to the model.
let
    Cleaned = Table.AddColumn(Files, "Data", each fnCleanFile([Content], [Extension], [Name]), type table)
in
    Cleaned
Loan_All · Power Query M
// Loan_All: every file's cleaned rows stacked into one table. Staging only: not loaded to the model.
let
    Combined = Table.Combine(Loan_Files[Data]),
    // The same PN twice on the same day (a re-sent file, two extracts for one date): keep the first,
    // which is the row from the newest file name because Files is sorted newest first.
    // Check_Files flags every date that has more than one file, so check those by hand.
    NoDupes = Table.Distinct(Combined, {"PN_No", "As_Of_Date"}),
    NoDate = Table.SelectRows(NoDupes, each [As_Of_Date] <> null)
in
    NoDate
Check_Files · Power Query M
// Check_Files: one row per file, read before duplicates are removed, so empty and re-sent files show.
// Read it after every refresh; not loaded to the model.
let
    PerFile = Table.AddColumn(Loan_Files, "Stats", each [
        As_Of_Date = List.Max([Data][As_Of_Date]),
        Rows = Table.RowCount([Data]),
        Total_Balance = List.Sum([Data][Outstanding_Balance]),
        Blank_Balance = List.Count(List.Select([Data][Outstanding_Balance], each _ = null)),
        No_PSIC = List.Count(List.Select([Data][PSIC_Section], each _ = "N/A"))]),
    Expanded = Table.ExpandRecordColumn(Table.SelectColumns(PerFile, {"Name", "Stats"}), "Stats",
        {"As_Of_Date", "Rows", "Total_Balance", "Blank_Balance", "No_PSIC"}),
    Typed = Table.TransformColumnTypes(Expanded, {{"Name", type text}, {"As_Of_Date", type date}, {"Rows", Int64.Type},
        {"Total_Balance", Currency.Type}, {"Blank_Balance", Int64.Type}, {"No_PSIC", Int64.Type}}),
    FilesPerDate = Table.AddColumn(Typed, "Files_Same_Date", each
        if [As_Of_Date] = null then null
        else Table.RowCount(Table.SelectRows(Typed, (r) => r[As_Of_Date] = [As_Of_Date])), Int64.Type),
    Sorted = Table.Sort(FilesPerDate, {{"As_Of_Date", Order.Descending}, {"Name", Order.Descending}})
in
    Sorted

Step 4 of 5 · Model + DAX

Data modelling: four tables, three relationships, 73 measures

Cut Loan_All into a star: one fact table of daily positions, two lookups (loans, industries) and a calendar of business days. All measures go in one table and are added in a single paste.

Picture Model view

Bold = key columns. Every relationship is one-to-many (1 → *), single direction: filters flow from Industry to Loans to LoanDaily, and from Dates to LoanDaily.

Do Steps

  1. Add four blank queries, Loans, LoanDaily, Dates and Industry, from the code below. These four are the only queries loaded. Close & Apply.
  2. File › Options › Current file › Data load: turn off Auto date/time.
  3. Model view: drag the three relationships in the table below. Check each one reads 1 to * and Single.
  4. Set the column settings below (sort-by columns, formats, hidden fields).
  5. Home › Enter data › name the table _Measures › Load. It holds the measures; hide its dummy column.
  6. DAX query view › paste the whole Measures block › click Update model with changes in the DAX query view ribbon (each MEASURE line also has its own "Update model: Add new measure" link). Then check the Data pane shows 73 measures under _Measures. Run shows the latest date and its book, but Run works even before the measures are saved, so the Data pane is the real check. If the button is missing in her version, add each MEASURE as New measure (name = text after _Measures[).
  7. Set formats with the format table (DAX query view does not carry them).
One side (1)Many side (*)Why
Industry[PSIC_Section]Loans[PSIC_Section]Industry labels, sort and colour reach each loan
Loans[PN_No]LoanDaily[PN_No]Branch, officer and product slicers reach the daily rows
Dates[Date]LoanDaily[As_Of_Date]Every date pick and axis
ColumnSetting
LoanDaily[DPD_Bucket]Sort by column DPD_Bucket_Sort
Dates[As_Of_Pick]Sort by column As_Of_Pick_Sort (puts "Latest" first)
Industry[Industry_Label]Sort by column Industry_Sort
Dates[Date] / Dates[Day]Format dd-mmm-yyyy (slicers) / d mmm (chart axes)
LoanDaily[Outstanding_Balance]Currency, ₱ Filipino (Philippines)
HideDPD_Bucket_Sort, As_Of_Pick_Sort, Industry_Sort, Industry_Colour, Week_Start, LoanDaily[PN_No], LoanDaily[As_Of_Date], Loans[PSIC_Section]

Why The logic

Balances are positions, so they are never added across days. ₱13.9bn on Monday plus ₱13.9bn on Tuesday is not ₱27.8bn. Every balance measure looks at exactly one date, [Selected Date] = MAX ( Dates[Date] ): the As-of pick, the end of a date range, or the point on a chart axis.

  • A star, not one wide table. The fact table keeps only the four columns that change daily. Branch, product and industry are stored once per loan, which keeps the file small and the slicers fast.
  • Dates holds business days only and is not marked as a date table. No time-intelligence functions are used. "Previous day" is the previous row, so Monday compares with Friday and a holiday never shows a fake zero.
  • Comparison dates are measures. [Prev Day Date] is the previous snapshot. [Week Ago Date] is the previous weekly snapshot on the Weekly page, and the latest day on or before d − 7 elsewhere. A Monday holiday cannot break "Monday to Monday".
  • New, Cured and Rolled are set operations on PN numbers: the PNs in 1–30 today EXCEPT or INTERSECT the PNs in each bucket at the comparison date. They respect every slicer and work per axis point.
  • "Latest" in the As-of slicer. A slicer saved on a fixed date stays there forever. Saved on the label "Latest", it moves to the newest day on each refresh.
  • Industry colours live in the data (Industry_Colour) and are applied with field-value formatting, so construction is the same colour on every chart, whatever its rank.
  • Dynamic format strings print ₱13.88bn and ₱137.8M from the same measure. The "bn" copies force one unit on trend charts so the axis does not flip between M and bn.

Code Model tables (Advanced Editor)

Loans · Power Query M
// Loans: one row per PN, with its latest Branch, Officer, Product and Industry
let
    Source = Loan_All,
    Latest = Table.Group(Source, {"PN_No"}, {{"Last", each Table.Max(_, "As_Of_Date"), type record}}),
    Expanded = Table.ExpandRecordColumn(Latest, "Last",
        {"Borrower_ID", "Branch", "Account_Officer", "Loan_Product", "PSIC_Section"}),
    Typed = Table.TransformColumnTypes(Expanded, {
        {"Borrower_ID", type text}, {"Branch", type text}, {"Account_Officer", type text},
        {"Loan_Product", type text}, {"PSIC_Section", type text}}),
    AddLabel = Table.AddColumn(Typed, "Account_Label", each Text.Combine({[PN_No], [Borrower_ID]}, " · "), type text)
in
    AddLabel
LoanDaily · Power Query M
// LoanDaily: the fact table, one row per PN per business day (an end-of-day position)
let
    Source = Table.SelectColumns(Loan_All, {"As_Of_Date", "PN_No", "Outstanding_Balance", "Days_Past_Due"}),
    OpenOnly = Table.SelectRows(Source, each [Outstanding_Balance] <> null and [Outstanding_Balance] > 0),
    AddBucket = Table.AddColumn(OpenOnly, "DPD_Bucket", each
        if [Days_Past_Due] <= 0 then "Current"
        else if [Days_Past_Due] <= 30 then "1-30"
        else if [Days_Past_Due] <= 60 then "31-60"
        else if [Days_Past_Due] <= 90 then "61-90"
        else "91+", type text),
    AddBucketSort = Table.AddColumn(AddBucket, "DPD_Bucket_Sort", each
        if [Days_Past_Due] <= 0 then 1
        else if [Days_Past_Due] <= 30 then 2
        else if [Days_Past_Due] <= 60 then 3
        else if [Days_Past_Due] <= 90 then 4
        else 5, Int64.Type),
    AddGroup = Table.AddColumn(AddBucketSort, "DPD_Group", each
        if [Days_Past_Due] <= 0 then "Current"
        else if [Days_Past_Due] <= 30 then "1-30 DPD"
        else "Over 30 DPD", type text)
in
    AddGroup
Dates · Power Query M
// Dates: one row per business day that exists in LoanDaily
let
    Source = Table.Distinct(Table.SelectColumns(LoanDaily, {"As_Of_Date"})),
    Renamed = Table.RenameColumns(Source, {{"As_Of_Date", "Date"}}),
    LatestDate = List.Max(Renamed[Date]),
    AddDay = Table.AddColumn(Renamed, "Day", each [Date], type date),
    AddWeekStart = Table.AddColumn(AddDay, "Week_Start", each Date.StartOfWeek([Date], Day.Monday), type date),
    FirstDayOfWeek = Table.Group(AddWeekStart, {"Week_Start"}, {{"Week_First_Date", each List.Min([Date]), type date}}),
    Joined = Table.NestedJoin(AddWeekStart, {"Week_Start"}, FirstDayOfWeek, {"Week_Start"}, "W", JoinKind.LeftOuter),
    Expanded = Table.ExpandTableColumn(Joined, "W", {"Week_First_Date"}),
    AddIsWeek = Table.AddColumn(Expanded, "Is_Week_Snapshot", each [Date] = [Week_First_Date], type logical),
    AddPick = Table.AddColumn(AddIsWeek, "As_Of_Pick", each
        if [Date] = LatestDate then "Latest" else Date.ToText([Date], [Format = "dd-MMM-yyyy", Culture = "en-US"]), type text),
    AddPickSort = Table.AddColumn(AddPick, "As_Of_Pick_Sort", each -Number.From([Date]), Int64.Type),
    Sorted = Table.Sort(Table.RemoveColumns(AddPickSort, {"Week_First_Date"}), {{"Date", Order.Ascending}}),
    Indexed = Table.AddIndexColumn(Sorted, "Idx", 0, 1, Int64.Type),
    RowCount = Table.RowCount(Indexed),
    AddDaysBack = Table.AddColumn(Indexed, "Bus_Days_Back", each RowCount - 1 - [Idx], Int64.Type),
    WeekDates = List.Sort(Table.SelectRows(AddDaysBack, each [Is_Week_Snapshot])[Date], Order.Descending),
    AddWeeksBack = Table.AddColumn(AddDaysBack, "Weeks_Back", each
        if [Is_Week_Snapshot] then List.PositionOf(WeekDates, [Date]) else null, Int64.Type),
    Result = Table.RemoveColumns(AddWeeksBack, {"Idx"})
in
    Result

DEFINE
    // ---- 3.1 Dates used by the comparisons
    MEASURE _Measures[Selected Date] =
        MAX ( Dates[Date] )

    MEASURE _Measures[Prev Day Date] =
        VAR _d = [Selected Date]
        RETURN
            CALCULATE ( MAX ( Dates[Date] ), REMOVEFILTERS ( Dates ), Dates[Date] < _d )

    MEASURE _Measures[Week Ago Date] =
        VAR _d = [Selected Date]
        RETURN
            IF (
                ISFILTERED ( Dates[Is_Week_Snapshot] ),
                CALCULATE ( MAX ( Dates[Date] ), REMOVEFILTERS ( Dates ), Dates[Is_Week_Snapshot] = TRUE (), Dates[Date] < _d ),
                CALCULATE ( MAX ( Dates[Date] ), REMOVEFILTERS ( Dates ), Dates[Date] <= _d - 7 )
            )

    // ---- 3.2 Core balances, counts and ratios
    MEASURE _Measures[Total Outstanding] =
        VAR _d = [Selected Date]
        RETURN
            CALCULATE (
                SUM ( LoanDaily[Outstanding_Balance] ),
                REMOVEFILTERS ( Dates ),
                Dates[Date] = _d
            )

    MEASURE _Measures[Loan Accounts] =
        VAR _d = [Selected Date]
        RETURN
            CALCULATE (
                DISTINCTCOUNT ( LoanDaily[PN_No] ),
                REMOVEFILTERS ( Dates ),
                Dates[Date] = _d
            )

    MEASURE _Measures[1-30 DPD Balance] =
        CALCULATE (
            [Total Outstanding],
            LoanDaily[Days_Past_Due] >= 1 && LoanDaily[Days_Past_Due] <= 30
        )

    MEASURE _Measures[1-30 DPD Accounts] =
        CALCULATE (
            [Loan Accounts],
            LoanDaily[Days_Past_Due] >= 1 && LoanDaily[Days_Past_Due] <= 30
        )

    MEASURE _Measures[1-30 DPD Ratio] =
        DIVIDE ( [1-30 DPD Balance], [Total Outstanding] )

    MEASURE _Measures[Over 30 DPD Balance] =
        CALCULATE ( [Total Outstanding], LoanDaily[Days_Past_Due] > 30 )

    MEASURE _Measures[Past Due Over 30 Ratio] =
        DIVIDE ( [Over 30 DPD Balance], [Total Outstanding] )

    MEASURE _Measures[1-30 DPD Balance bn] =
        [1-30 DPD Balance]

    MEASURE _Measures[Total Outstanding bn] =
        [Total Outstanding]

    // ---- 3.3 Same numbers for the comparison day
    MEASURE _Measures[1-30 DPD Balance (Prev Day)] =
        VAR _p = [Prev Day Date]
        RETURN
            IF (
                NOT ISBLANK ( _p ),
                CALCULATE ( [1-30 DPD Balance], REMOVEFILTERS ( Dates ), Dates[Date] = _p )
            )

    MEASURE _Measures[1-30 DPD Ratio (Prev Day)] =
        VAR _p = [Prev Day Date]
        RETURN
            IF (
                NOT ISBLANK ( _p ),
                CALCULATE ( [1-30 DPD Ratio], REMOVEFILTERS ( Dates ), Dates[Date] = _p )
            )

    MEASURE _Measures[Total Outstanding (Week Ago)] =
        VAR _p = [Week Ago Date]
        RETURN
            IF (
                NOT ISBLANK ( _p ),
                CALCULATE ( [Total Outstanding], REMOVEFILTERS ( Dates ), Dates[Date] = _p )
            )

    MEASURE _Measures[1-30 DPD Balance (Week Ago)] =
        VAR _p = [Week Ago Date]
        RETURN
            IF (
                NOT ISBLANK ( _p ),
                CALCULATE ( [1-30 DPD Balance], REMOVEFILTERS ( Dates ), Dates[Date] = _p )
            )

    MEASURE _Measures[1-30 DPD Ratio (Week Ago)] =
        VAR _p = [Week Ago Date]
        RETURN
            IF (
                NOT ISBLANK ( _p ),
                CALCULATE ( [1-30 DPD Ratio], REMOVEFILTERS ( Dates ), Dates[Date] = _p )
            )

    MEASURE _Measures[Past Due Over 30 Ratio (Week Ago)] =
        VAR _p = [Week Ago Date]
        RETURN
            IF (
                NOT ISBLANK ( _p ),
                CALCULATE ( [Past Due Over 30 Ratio], REMOVEFILTERS ( Dates ), Dates[Date] = _p )
            )

    // ---- 3.4 Changes (numbers; used for red/green colours and the loan product chart)
    MEASURE _Measures[Chg 1-30 Balance (Day)] =
        IF (
            NOT ISBLANK ( [Prev Day Date] ),
            [1-30 DPD Balance] - [1-30 DPD Balance (Prev Day)]
        )

    MEASURE _Measures[Chg 1-30 Ratio pts (Day)] =
        IF (
            NOT ISBLANK ( [Prev Day Date] ),
            ( [1-30 DPD Ratio] - [1-30 DPD Ratio (Prev Day)] ) * 100
        )

    MEASURE _Measures[Chg 1-30 Balance (Week)] =
        IF (
            NOT ISBLANK ( [Week Ago Date] ),
            [1-30 DPD Balance] - [1-30 DPD Balance (Week Ago)]
        )

    MEASURE _Measures[Chg 1-30 Ratio pts (Week)] =
        IF (
            NOT ISBLANK ( [Week Ago Date] ),
            ( [1-30 DPD Ratio] - [1-30 DPD Ratio (Week Ago)] ) * 100
        )

    MEASURE _Measures[Chg Over 30 Ratio pts (Week)] =
        IF (
            NOT ISBLANK ( [Week Ago Date] ),
            ( [Past Due Over 30 Ratio] - [Past Due Over 30 Ratio (Week Ago)] ) * 100
        )

    MEASURE _Measures[Chg Total Outstanding % (Week)] =
        DIVIDE (
            [Total Outstanding] - [Total Outstanding (Week Ago)],
            [Total Outstanding (Week Ago)]
        )

    // ---- 3.5 Small text lines under the big card numbers ("reference labels")
    MEASURE _Measures[Ref 1-30 Balance (Day)] =
        VAR _c = [Chg 1-30 Balance (Day)]
        VAR _a = ABS ( _c )
        RETURN
            IF (
                NOT ISBLANK ( _c ),
                IF ( _c >= 0, "▲ +₱", "▼ −₱" )
                    & IF ( _a >= 1000000000, FORMAT ( _a / 1000000000, "#,0.00" ) & "bn", FORMAT ( _a / 1000000, "#,0.0" ) & "M" )
                    & " vs " & FORMAT ( [Prev Day Date], "d mmm" )
            )

    MEASURE _Measures[Ref 1-30 Ratio (Day)] =
        VAR _c = [Chg 1-30 Ratio pts (Day)]
        RETURN
            IF (
                NOT ISBLANK ( _c ),
                IF ( _c >= 0, "▲ +", "▼ −" ) & FORMAT ( ABS ( _c ), "0.0" ) & " pts vs "
                    & FORMAT ( [Prev Day Date], "d mmm" )
            )

    MEASURE _Measures[Ref 1-30 Balance (Week)] =
        VAR _c = [Chg 1-30 Balance (Week)]

            IF (

                    & IF ( ISFILTERED ( Dates[Is_Week_Snapshot] ), " vs week of ", " vs " ) & FORMAT ( [Week Ago Date], "d mmm" )
            )

    MEASURE _Measures[Ref 1-30 Ratio (Week)] =
        VAR _c = [Chg 1-30 Ratio pts (Week)]
        RETURN
            IF (
                NOT ISBLANK ( _c ),
                IF ( _c >= 0, "▲ +", "▼ −" ) & FORMAT ( ABS ( _c ), "0.0" ) & " pts"
                    & IF ( ISFILTERED ( Dates[Is_Week_Snapshot] ), " vs week of ", " vs " )
                    & FORMAT ( [Week Ago Date], "d mmm" )
            )

    MEASURE _Measures[Ref Over 30 Ratio (Week)] =
        VAR _c = [Chg Over 30 Ratio pts (Week)]
        RETURN
            IF (
                NOT ISBLANK ( _c ),
                IF ( _c >= 0, "▲ +", "▼ −" ) & FORMAT ( ABS ( _c ), "0.0" ) & " pts"
                    & IF ( ISFILTERED ( Dates[Is_Week_Snapshot] ), " vs week of ", " vs " )

            )

    MEASURE _Measures[Ref Total Outstanding (Week)] =

        RETURN

                    & FORMAT ( [Week Ago Date], "d mmm" )
            )

    MEASURE _Measures[Ref Loan Accounts] =
        FORMAT ( [Loan Accounts], "#,0" ) & " loan accounts"

    MEASURE _Measures[Ref 1-30 Accounts] =

    // ---- 3.6 Accounts moving in and out of 1-30 days past due
    MEASURE _Measures[New to 1-30 (Day)] =

        RETURN

    MEASURE _Measures[1-30 DPD Ratio All Industries] =

            )
        RETURN
            MAXX ( TOPN ( 1, _t, [@ratio], DESC ), Industry[Industry_Label] )

                )
            ) + 0

        "Loans 1–30 days past due vs total outstanding loans · as of " & FORMAT ( [Selected Date], "d mmm yyyy" )

    MEASURE _Measures[Subtitle Industry] =
        "Loans 1–30 days past due vs total outstanding, by PSIC industry · as of " & FORMAT ( [Selected Date], "d mmm yyyy" )

    MEASURE _Measures[Subtitle Daily] =
        "Whole loan book, business days · latest " & FORMAT ( [Selected Date], "d mmm yyyy" )

    MEASURE _Measures[Subtitle Weekly] =
        "Whole loan book, Monday positions · latest week of " & FORMAT ( [Selected Date], "d mmm yyyy" )

    MEASURE _Measures[Title Daily Balance Card] =
        "1–30 DPD Balance, " & FORMAT ( [Selected Date], "d mmm" )

    MEASURE _Measures[Title Daily DPD Chart] =
        "Outstanding Balance by Days Past Due, " & FORMAT ( [Selected Date], "d mmm" )

    MEASURE _Measures[Title Weekly Branch Chart] =
        "1–30 DPD Ratio by Branch, Week of " & FORMAT ( [Selected Date], "d mmm" )
            & " vs " & FORMAT ( [Week Ago Date], "d mmm" )

    MEASURE _Measures[Title Weekly Product Chart] =
        "Change in 1–30 DPD Balance by Loan Product vs Week of " & FORMAT ( [Week Ago Date], "d mmm" )

    MEASURE _Measures[Last 5 Days Flag] =
        VAR _d = MAX ( Dates[Date] )
        VAR _laterDays =
            CALCULATE (
                COUNTROWS ( Dates ),
                ALLSELECTED ( Dates ),
                KEEPFILTERS ( Dates[Date] > _d )
            )
        RETURN
            IF ( _laterDays < 5, 1, 0 )

// Test: shows the latest day's headline numbers once "Update model" has added the measures
EVALUATE
    ROW (
        "Selected Date", [Selected Date],
        "Total Outstanding", [Total Outstanding],
        "1-30 DPD Balance", [1-30 DPD Balance],
        "1-30 DPD Ratio", [1-30 DPD Ratio]
    )

Format Measure formats

MeasuresFormat
Selected Date, Prev Day Date, Week Ago DateCustom d mmm
Total Outstanding, 1-30 DPD Balance, Over 30 DPD BalanceDynamic, with the Balance format string below. Older Desktop without Dynamic: Currency ₱ and set display units per visual.
1-30 DPD Balance bn, Total Outstanding bnCustom "₱"#,0.00,,,"bn"
All Ratio measures, incl. (Prev Day), (Week Ago), All Industries, Highest Industry RatioPercentage, 1 decimal
Loan Accounts, 1-30 DPD Accounts, all New / Cured / Rolled countsWhole number, thousands separator
(Prev Day) and (Week Ago) balances, New / Cured / Rolled BalanceCurrency ₱
Chg 1-30 Balance (Day), (Week)Custom +"₱"#,0.0,,"M";-"₱"#,0.0,,"M";"₱0.0M"
Chg … Ratio ptsDecimal number, 1 decimal
Chg Total Outstanding % (Week)Percentage, 1 decimal
1-30 DPD Balance (Share)Dynamic, with the Share format string below (treemap labels "₱308.6M · 31%")
Format_Balance · DAX
IF (
    ABS ( SELECTEDMEASURE () ) >= 1000000000,
    """₱""#,0.00,,,""bn""",
    """₱""#,0.0,,""M"""
)
Format_Share · DAX
VAR _v = [1-30 DPD Balance]
VAR _share = DIVIDE ( _v, CALCULATE ( [1-30 DPD Balance], REMOVEFILTERS ( Industry ) ) )
VAR _scale = IF ( ABS ( _v ) >= 1000000000, "#,0.00,,,", "#,0.0,," )
VAR _unit = IF ( ABS ( _v ) >= 1000000000, "bn", "M" )
RETURN
    """₱""" & _scale & """" & _unit & " · " & FORMAT ( _share, "0%" ) & """"

Step 5 of 5 · Report

Power BI charts: four pages, built element by element

Each page below has its picture with yellow IDs and a table giving every element's position on the 1280 × 720 canvas, its fields and its settings. Build the header once, then copy it to each page.

Do Steps

  1. Save the theme below as delinquency-theme.json › View › Themes › Browse for themes.
  2. Canvas 16:9, 1280 × 720. Header bar (H): rectangle 0, 0, 1280, 52 in #1B2A4A, title text box in white Segoe UI Semibold 14, subtitle card bound to the page's Subtitle measure.
  3. Sample badge (B) until real data is loaded; page navigator (N) at 880, 12, 388, 28. Paste H, B and N on all four pages.
  4. Cards (K) are Card (new): callout 20 pt, display units None so the measure's format applies; reference label = the Ref measure; red / green by rules on the Chg measure (> 0 #C4314B, ≤ 0 #107C10). 1–30 cards get a 3 px #E66C37 accent bar.
  5. Build each page from its table. Page order and names: Overview, Industry, Daily, Weekly.
  6. Sync slicers: Branch, Loan product and Account officer on all four pages; Industry and As-of date on Overview and Industry only; the Daily Date and Weekly Week-of slicers stay on their own page.

Code Theme file

theme · JSON
{
  "name": "Early Delinquency Watch",
  "dataColors": ["#118DFF", "#12239E", "#E66C37", "#6B007B", "#E044A7", "#744EC2", "#D9B300", "#D64550", "#197278", "#1AAB40"],
  "foreground": "#252423",
  "background": "#FFFFFF",
  "tableAccent": "#118DFF",
  "good": "#107C10",
  "neutral": "#605E5C",
  "bad": "#C4314B",
  "textClasses": {
    "callout": { "fontSize": 20, "fontFace": "Segoe UI Semibold", "color": "#252423" },
    "title":   { "fontSize": 11, "fontFace": "Segoe UI Semibold", "color": "#252423" },
    "header":  { "fontSize": 9,  "fontFace": "Segoe UI Semibold", "color": "#252423" },
    "label":   { "fontSize": 9,  "fontFace": "Segoe UI", "color": "#605E5C" }
  },
  "visualStyles": {
    "page": {
      "*": {
        "background": [ { "color": { "solid": { "color": "#EFF1F4" } }, "transparency": 0 } ]
      }
    },
    "*": {
      "*": {
        "background": [ { "show": true, "color": { "solid": { "color": "#FFFFFF" } }, "transparency": 0 } ],
        "border": [ { "show": false, "radius": 4 } ],
        "dropShadow": [ { "show": false } ]
      }
    }
  }
}
ColourHexMeans
Orange#E66C37Everything 1–30 DPD
Blue#118DFFCurrent (0 DPD)
Navy#12239EOver 30 DPD, rolled to 31+, "this week"
Light blue#9CCBFFTotal outstanding, "last week"
Red#D64550New to 1–30, balance up (worse)
Green#1AAB40Cured, balance down (better)
Card text#C4314B / #107C10Same worse / better meaning as red and green, darker so small card text stays readable

Why The logic

Four pages, four questions. Overview: where are we today against a week ago? Industry: which sectors carry the early delinquency? Daily: what moved since yesterday? Weekly: is it a trend or noise?

  • One colour, one meaning, on every page. Orange is always 1–30 DPD; red is always worse; green is always better. A manager never has to read a legend twice.
  • Cards carry the comparison under the number. A ratio of 4.1% means nothing alone; "▲ +0.3 pts vs 12 Oct" tells the reader which way to look.
  • Daily and Weekly cover the whole book with no industry slicer: they answer "is the bank getting worse", and Industry answers "where".
  • Page filters move with each refresh (last 15 business days, last 12 weeks), so the report never needs re-saving to stay current.
  • Top 10 by balance, labelled PN No. · Borrower ID: the list the collection head acts on, with no borrower names on a management page.

Check Before anyone sees it

  1. [Total Outstanding] for a day equals the core-banking / GL loan total for that day.
  2. [1-30 DPD Balance] equals the 1–30 bucket of the bank's aging report.
  3. Check three PNs' DPD by hand against the source file named in Source_File.
  4. New + Cured + Rolled will not exactly equal the change in the 1–30 count: loans also leave by payoff or come back from over 30. That is expected.

After Step 5 · Analysis

Reading the dashboard: what each chart tells management

For each visual: the question it answers, what a worrying reading looks like, and the next question to ask. Then the patterns to watch across pages.

Page Overview

Where the book stands today against the same day last week.

K2 · K3 1–30 DPD balance and ratio

Answers
How much of the book has started to slip, in pesos and as a share.
Worrying sign
Balance up while the ratio is flat or down: the book grew and hid the slippage. Read the peso change before the ratio.
Ask next
Is the rise in a few big PNs (Top 10) or spread across many?

K5 Past due over 30 ratio

Answers
How much is already past early warning.
Worrying sign
Over 30 rising about four weeks after 1–30 rose (a loan has to age through the 30-day bucket first): accounts are rolling forward, not curing.
Ask next
Which product and branch feed the roll? Open Daily V2 for the Rolled bar.

V1 Balance by DPD bucket

Answers
The ageing shape of the whole book.
Worrying sign
The 31–60 and 61–90 bars thickening week on week: the 1–30 bucket is feeding later buckets.
Ask next
How many of today's 31–60 were in 1–30 a month ago?

V2 1–30 ratio by branch

Answers
Which branches carry early delinquency relative to their size.
Worrying sign
One branch far above the rest for several weeks, not one day.
Ask next
Same officer, same product, or same borrower group behind it?

V3 Top 10 accounts 1–30

Answers
The PNs where one call changes the number.
Worrying sign
The same PN in the Top 10 for more than a month (5+ weekly snapshots): partial payments keep resetting its DPD, a chronic one-instalment-behind account.
Ask next
What is the borrower's payment capacity, and has the AO logged a promise to pay or a visit?

V4 1–30 balance by product

Answers
Which products drive the early-delinquency pesos.
Worrying sign
A product's share of 1–30 much higher than its share of the book.
Ask next
Is it a recent batch of releases? The release dates are in the source extract.

Page Industry

Which PSIC sectors carry the early delinquency.

V1 1–30 ratio by industry

Answers
Which sectors pay late relative to their size; the dashed line is the all-industry ratio.
Worrying sign
A sector moving from below the line to above it, or staying above it for a month.
Ask next
Is it seasonal (agriculture before harvest) or a real change in the sector?

V2 Share of 1–30 balance (treemap)

Answers
Where the early-delinquency pesos sit.
Worrying sign
One sector holding most of the 1–30 pesos: a concentration, whatever its ratio.
Ask next
What is our total exposure to that sector, including undrawn lines?

V3 1–30 vs total by industry

Answers
Exposure and slippage side by side.
Worrying sign
A large sector with a modest ratio: a 1-point rise there moves more pesos than a big rise in a small sector.
Ask next
How many pesos would move to 1–30 if its ratio rose 1 point?

K4 · K5 Highest ratio, sectors above

Answers
How broad the problem is.
Worrying sign
The count of sectors above the all-industry ratio rising: the slippage is spreading, not concentrated.
Ask next
Is the cause macro (rates, a typhoon area) rather than sector-specific?

Page Daily

What moved since the previous business day.

K3 · K4 · K5 New, Cured, Rolled today

Answers
The flows behind the change in the 1–30 balance.
Worrying sign
New above Cured for five business days running, or any jump in Rolled.
Ask next
Which PNs rolled? They are the next NPL candidates.

V1 Daily 1–30 balance

Answers
The day-to-day path.
Worrying sign
A step up that does not come back down after the next payment date.
Ask next
Did a due-date cluster (15th, 30th) just pass? Compare with the same point last month.

V2 In and out, last 5 days

Answers
Whether cures keep pace with new arrivals.
Worrying sign
Red bars taller than green on most days.
Ask next
Are cures coming from full payment or from restructuring?

V4 Top 10 accounts 1–30

Answers
Today's action list for collection.
Worrying sign
A new PN entering high on the list in one day: a large account just missed.
Ask next
Who is the AO, and is there a known reason (dispute, delayed remittance)?

Page Weekly

Whether the movement is a trend or noise.

V1 Weekly 1–30 balance

Answers
The 12-week trend on the same weekday. It removes day-of-week noise, not the payday cycle: a Monday just after the 15th reads higher than the Monday before it.
Worrying sign
The 4-week direction rising, or this point above the same point last month (for example the first Monday after the 15th).
Ask next
Is the book growing at the same pace? If not, the ratio will follow.

V2 In and out, Monday to Monday

Answers
Net flow into 1–30 each week.
Worrying sign
Rolled to 31+ growing week on week even when New is flat: the early bucket is ageing.
Ask next
What is the weekly cure rate (Cured ÷ last week's 1–30 accounts)?

V3 Ratio by branch, last vs this week

Answers
Which branches improved or worsened this week.
Worrying sign
Navy bar above light blue for the same branches two weeks running.
Ask next
Did those branches change AO or push a product recently?

V4 Change in 1–30 balance by product

Answers
Which products drove the week's change.
Worrying sign
One product red every week.
Ask next
Tighten approval or collection for that product, or is it one large account?

Why Patterns to watch across pages

  • 1–30 DPD is the early-warning bucket. What matters is where it goes next. Watch Rolled to 31+ more closely than the 1–30 balance itself: rolls are the leading indicator of NPLs.
  • The ratio has a denominator. A growing book lowers the ratio with no improvement in payment behaviour. Always read the peso balance next to the ratio.
  • Due dates cluster. Where amortisations are set to paydays (mostly consumer and salary loans), DPD jumps the day after the 15th and month-end, then cures over the following days. Neither day-on-day nor week-on-week holds the cycle constant: compare with the same point last month, or read the 4-week direction, before reacting to a jump.
  • Concentration beats rate. A few large PNs can move the whole ratio. If the Top 10 holds a big share of the 1–30 balance, the story is about those accounts, not the portfolio.
  • Persistence is the signal. One bad day is noise; three weeks in the same direction is a trend worth an agenda line.

Pack Five questions for the weekly management note

  1. Did the 1–30 balance and ratio rise or fall versus last week, and was it the book or the slippage?
  2. How many accounts rolled to 31+ this week, and which products and branches?
  3. Which industry is furthest above the all-industry ratio, and for how many weeks?
  4. Which Top 10 accounts are new this week, and what is the collection plan for each?
  5. Is the cure rate keeping up with new arrivals?
